comments.body: Congratulations on your first merged pull request!

review_comments.body: If these adjustments have a rule (e.g., a holiday on Saturday or Sunday falls on the next Monday) they can be written as a general rule instead of ad-hoc additional days; see, for instance, the way that New Year's Day is adjusted in the Australian calendar at https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/blob/v1.44/ql/time/calendars/australia.cpp#L49-L50

Done, thanks. The rule is point 3 of the DGPA guidelines that implement article 8 of the Act (https://www.dgpa.gov.tw/information?uid=84&pid=12576): a holiday falling on a Saturday is made up on the previous working day and one falling on a Sunday on the next one, so the three new holidays now move to Friday or Monday and the ad-hoc 2025/2026 days are gone (I also added a check for December 24th, 2027, which is off in the 2027 government calendar). The same rule applies to the other fixed holidays too; I left those alone here, but I can do the same for them if you'd like.
Yes, please, let's fix the other rules as well.  Thanks!

Done, thanks. The same rule has applied to the other fixed holidays since 2015 (article 5-1 of the previous Regulations on the Implementation of Commemorative Days and Holidays, https://law.moj.gov.tw/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?pcode=D0020033), so New Year's Day, Peace Memorial Day, Labor Day and National Day now follow it from 2015 on, and the ad-hoc days it covers in 2015-2026 are gone. The holidays up to 2026 don't change, and the new ones for 2027 (March 1st, April 30th, October 11th and December 31st) match the DGPA 2027 calendar. Children's Day and Tomb Sweeping Day are still listed by year, since the latter doesn't fall on a fixed date. I updated the PR description too.

title: Add Teachers' Day, Retrocession Day and Constitution Day to Taiwan calendar
